info.title: Core Admin API
info.description: Core Admin — the platform operator console's own API (operator bearer token, `Authorization: Bearer <token>`). This is not a third-party integration surface; see `/docs/api` for that.

get.description:
Optionally scoped to a `project_id`. Requires `webhooks:read`.

ADR-0069 §2 — the account's scope always applies on top of the
requested project: a `project_id` outside the scope yields an empty
page, and the unfiltered listing only shows the account's projects.

Polls `checkStatus()` on a small batch of payments stuck in a
non-terminal status, applying any status change through the same
path an inbound webhook uses. Requires `payments:reconcile:write`.

admin listing (payments, wallets, notifications) starts from a
`project_id` found here. Requires `projects:read`.

post.description:
The response carries the **activation token**, once. The account
does not exist yet: the invitee chooses their own password when
they activate the invitation
(`POST /v1/admin/operator-invitations/accept`) — no password is
chosen by the system and none is transmitted (ADR-0081 S-07), the
same one-shot-secret pattern as the API key issuance, applied to
the console account itself.

Requires `operators:write` (Platform Admin only). MFA enrollment
happens on first login, not here.
post.summary: Invite an email address to hold a console account

role.description:
ADR-0069 §1 — an empty role means an account without a
platform role, living in its organizations only.

put.description:
Never touches credentials or MFA state — those are separate flows.
Requires `operators:write` (Platform Admin only). Audits internally
— `identity` has `audit` module access. Returns 204 — the port
returns void.

role.description:
ADR-0069 §1 — the platform role is optional: an empty role
means "no platform role at all" (the account keeps only its
organization memberships). The key must still be present, so
a partial update never clears the role by accident.

post.description:
Idempotent — revoking an already-revoked operator succeeds without
effect. Requires `operators:write` (Platform Admin only). A
revoked operator's existing bearer tokens are rejected on their
very next request (`ResolveOperatorFromBearerToken` re-checks
revocation every time), so this takes effect immediately.

post.description:
Public endpoint — the invitation token is the only thing that
grants access: the invitee is not signed in yet. Consumes the
token (one-shot, 72 h) and creates the account with the password
the invitee **chooses**.

name.description: The display name of the account.

password.description:
ADR-0069 §4 — the password the invitee chooses (the system
never chooses one, never transmits one). The length rule
is the use case's, so the refusal is a 422 of its own.

post.description:
Returns a short-lived challenge token and a `purpose` telling the
caller which endpoint to call next — `mfa_enrollment` on first login,
`mfa` once MFA is already enabled. When `IDENTITY_DISABLE_MFA=true`
the MFA step is skipped entirely and the response carries the
issued bearer token directly. That flag is NOT env-gated — every
runtime where it's set behaves this way, including production if
someone misconfigures it. The expected use is development / pilot.
post.summary: Step 1 of operator login: verify email and password
